outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Paradigm Shift from Post-Training Quantization to 1-bit Architectures
outline.description: An introduction to the challenges of deploying Large Language Models (LLMs), including memory bottlenecks, energy consumption, and FP16 inefficiency. This chapter contrasts standard post-training quantization with the architectural shift required for true 1-bit models, establishing the theoretical motivation for BitNet b1.58.
subtopics: The Scaling Challenges of LLMs: Memory Bandwidth and Energy Constraints
Post-Training Quantization (PTQ): History, GPTQ/SmoothQuant, and Fundamental Limits
Why Post-Training is Sub-optimal: The Cost of Re-discovering Precision
From Bits to Architecture: Theoretical Benefits of Integer Arithmetic
The Memory Bottleneck Problem: DRAM vs. SRAM Trade-offs
Introduction to 1-bit Computing Paradigms

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Anatomy of BitNet b1.58 and Ternary Parameterization
outline.description: A deep dive into the specific design choices that constitute BitNet b1.58. This section explains how ternary parameters {-1, 0, 1} differ from binary parameters and why the inclusion of zero is critical for performance and feature filtering.
subtopics: Ternary vs. Binary Weights: The Significance of the Zero State
Mathematical Foundation: Representing 1-bit in 1.58 Bits (Entropy Calculation)
BitLinear Layer Design: Eliminating Matrix Multiplication via Integer Addition Convolution
The Absmean Quantization Function: Scaling Logic without Width Squeezing
Activation Quantization: Why We Use 8-bit Activations and Zero Constants
Bias Nomalization and Weight Initialization Strategies for Ternary Models

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: LLaMA-alike Compatibility and Software Implementation
outline.description: This chapter addresses the practical adoption of BitNet b1.58 by detailing its adherence to standard open-source architectures. It covers the specific components adopted from LLaMA (RMSNorm, SwiGLU) and provides guidance on integration into popular toolchains.
